intro: Chi-square tests handle counts in categories. The statistic is $\chi^2=\sum\dfrac{(O-E)^2}{E}$, summing over cells, where $O$ is the observed and $E$ the expected count under $H_0$. The goodness-of-fit test compares one categorical variable to a claimed distribution (df $=$ categories $-1$). Tests of homogeneity/independence use a two-way table with expected count $E=\dfrac{(\text{row total})(\text{column total})}{\text{grand total}}$ and df $=(\text{rows}-1)(\text{columns}-1)$. Large $\chi^2$ gives a small p-value.

items.prompt: One cell has observed $O=30$ and expected $E=25$. Find its contribution to $\chi^2$.
A goodness-of-fit test has $5$ categories. State the degrees of freedom.

steps: For goodness of fit, df $=$ categories $-1$.

items.prompt: Find the expected count for a cell with row total $40$, column total $30$, grand total $120$.
